subject: RelayBuffer: regional relay addition (subprocessor amendment) — action requested
messages:
From: RelayBuffer Ops <ops@relaybuffer.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Subprocessor amendment: EU relay node (limited caching)

Hi Jasmine,

Quick heads up: RelayBuffer is adding a lightweight relay node in Amsterdam to reduce egress latency for EU customers. The node performs limited request buffering and transient caching (<1 hour) and is operated by our partner RelayEdge B.V. We expect the change to go live on 2027-09-15.

What this impacts for Redwood:
- Subprocessor: RelayEdge B.V. (Netherlands) will handle network-level buffering for certain EU-region traffic.
- Data residency: No long-term storage — ephemeral buffers only, KV entries expire within an hour.
- Purpose: latency optimization and packet reassembly; no customer PII persists beyond buffer TTL.

We attach the updated subprocessor roster and a SOC2 summary for RelayEdge. Please confirm whether you need a DPA addendum or a short signature to acknowledge this roster update. If you want, we can push a DocuSign amendment and provide a brief dataflow diagram.

Attachments: relaybuffer_subprocessors_2027-08.csv (csv), SOC2_summary_2027.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Taylor Chen
Ops — RelayBuffer
[Attachment: relaybuffer_subprocessors_2027-08.csv]
[Attachment: SOC2_summary_2027.pdf]

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: RelayBuffer Ops <ops@relaybuffer.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-29T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor amendment: EU relay node (limited caching)

Hi Taylor,

Thanks for the notice. A couple of quick clarifying questions before I loop Legal and Security:

1) Can you confirm the exact fields that may traverse the buffer (token IDs, request headers, request body) and whether any unredacted PII could be present in request bodies?
2) Is RelayEdge listed as a subprocessor in your DPA with the same security controls as RelayBuffer, or will we need a small DPA addendum?
3) Can you provide the dataflow diagram as a PNG and a link to the DocuSign amendment so our procurement team can triage?

Marissa / Jonas — FYI. Marissa, if this is operational only and buffers are ephemeral we may be able to handle this as a roster acknowledgement; if RelayEdge requires additional contractual language I’ll ask Legal to prepare a short addendum. Jonas — please flag any red-team / observability requirements.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Partner Security Liaison
Redwood Inference

From: RelayBuffer Security <security@relaybuffer.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: RelayBuffer Ops <ops@relaybuffer.ai>
Date: 2027-08-29T14:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor amendment: EU relay node (limited caching)

On Mon, Aug 29, 2027 at 11:04 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the notice. A couple of quick clarifying questions before I loop Legal and Security:
>
> 1) Can you confirm the exact fields that may traverse the buffer (token IDs, request headers, request body) and whether any unredacted PII could be present in request bodies?
> 2) Is RelayEdge listed as a subprocessor in your DPA with the same security controls as RelayBuffer, or will we need a small DPA addendum?
> 3) Can you provide the dataflow diagram as a PNG and a link to the DocuSign amendment so our procurement team can triage?

Hi Jasmine — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers up front:
1) Fields: headers + request body may transit the buffer. We are not intentionally persisting user identifiers; however, request bodies sometimes include customer content (prompts/requests). RelayEdge's configuration actively strips authentication headers and applies masking on recognized PII tokens before buffering. We call out the masking rules in the attached CSV.
2) RelayEdge is a subcontractor and is covered under our DPA via an addendum (we've included the relevant clause excerpts in SOC2_summary_2027.pdf). If Redwood requires a countersignature we can route a one-page addendum via DocuSign.
3) Dataflow diagram: https://drive.google.com/relaybuffer/onboard-diagram
   DocuSign (optional countersign): https://docusign.com/relaybuffer/amendment/abc123

Also noting: RelayEdge only accepts TLS 1.2+ with mutual auth for buffer endpoints, and they run ephemeral storage on encrypted disks with a 60-minute TTL. We can provide network peering logs for the go-live window if you want to validate.

Attachments included again: relaybuffer_subprocessors_2027-08.csv, SOC2_summary_2027.pdf

— Samir Patel
Security Lead — RelayBuffer
[Attachment: SOC2_summary_2027.pdf]
[Attachment: relaybuffer_subprocessors_2027-08.csv]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-08-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Subprocessor amendment: EU relay node (limited caching)

Thanks for the thread and the attachments.

Jasmine — please kick Legal on the DocuSign addendum if they prefer countersigning; otherwise classify this as a roster acknowledgement and record RelayEdge under the supplier list with a note: "ephemeral buffer, TTL=60m, masks PII, TLS mutual-auth."

Jonas — confirm that observability hooks (peering logs + buf metrics) will be ingested into our monitoring sandbox and that we have alerting for unexpected retention events. If those checks look good, procurement can process the acknowledgement and close the ticket.

I'll approve the acknowledgement path once Legal confirms the addendum language is not required.

Marissa Cole
Director, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
